des_teaser.label: Teaser hero — empty country radio studio

content.prompt: Cinematic dimly lit empty country radio studio at night. Vintage on-air microphone in soft amber spotlight, two vinyl records hanging on the wall edge-on so they cannot touch. Neon 'On Air' sign glowing red softly. Dark moody editorial photography. 35mm film grain. No text in frame.

des_teaser.brief: Full-bleed hero. Two records hanging edge-on, deliberately not touching, is the visual metaphor for the back-to-back finding. The On-Air sign and microphone establish 'this is country radio.' No people, no text — let the metaphor land before the title.
des_teaser.rationale: An interactive teaser would dilute the punch of the headline. A single cinematic image — two records that can't touch — telegraphs the entire blog before the reader scrolls.

des_01.label: Headline gap chart — 65% vs 0.5%

content.interaction: hover tooltip with exact b2b_count and pct_of_all_plays; the Women bar is annotated inline with 'two records that almost never touch'

des_01.brief: Three horizontal bars. Men → Men is overwhelmingly long (65.01%). Mixed → Mixed (0.47%) and Women → Women (0.51%) are tiny slivers — almost invisible by comparison. Use the same x-axis scale for all three; do NOT use a broken/log axis. The visual asymmetry IS the finding. Annotate the Women bar with the exact count '928 plays' and the Men bar with '118,861 plays' on the bar itself.
des_01.rationale: A pie chart or split bar would soften the asymmetry. A single shared x-axis with all three categories at honest scale makes the 128:1 ratio jaw-droppingly visible.

des_02.label: Stat callout — 128 to 1

content.label: men back-to-back vs women back-to-back, on country radio in 2022

des_02.brief: Massive serif number set just under the hero, before the prose. Render as '128 : 1' in 96px display serif (warm bone-white on near-black background) with the smaller subtitle below it.
des_02.rationale: The ratio is the single most quotable artefact of the analysis. Place it directly in the hook so it lodges before context.

des_03.label: Airplay share donut — 81/10/8

content.interaction: hover slice shows count + pct; clicking 'Women' slice triggers a small inset chart that shows what fraction of women's plays were back-to-back (using ana_01's 928 / 18,412)

des_03.brief: Donut chart split into three slices: men 81.5%, women 10.1%, mixed 8.4%. The Women slice is highlighted in tomato red. Below the donut: a tiny secondary visualization showing 928 / 18,412 = 5% — i.e., even within women's airplay only 5% of plays land next to another woman.
des_03.rationale: This section's argument is layered: the casting decision (10%) on top of the programming decision (5% of those 10%). A donut + sub-stat captures both layers without crowding.

des_04.label: P-value lollipop — 25 of 29 stations significant

content.interaction: hover shows city, station, owner, exact p-value; vertical dashed reference line at p=0.05

des_04.brief: Vertical lollipop list of all 29 stations, sorted by p-value ascending. Stations with p=0 (18 of them) cluster at the left as a wall of red dots flush against the y-axis. A dashed vertical rule at p=0.05 separates 'statistically anomalous' (left, red) from 'within chance' (right, grey, only 4 stations: KAJA, WUSN, KASE, WTQR). Annotate '18 stations: observed below ALL 1,000 random shuffles'.
des_04.rationale: P-values look intimidating, but a lollipop sorted ascending makes the wall of zeros pre-attentive — readers see 'almost all stations' before they read 'p=0'.

des_05.label: Station leaderboard — bar chart with city annotations

content.interaction: hover shows full row (city, owner, b2b_women_count, total_plays). Tooltip phrasing: 'X paired women back-to-back N times in M sampled plays'

des_05.brief: 29 horizontal bars sorted descending. The top bar (KKGO-LA, 1.27%) and the bottom bar (WUBE-Cincinnati, 0.03%) are color-emphasized in red and dark slate respectively. Bars are colored by owner so readers can spot owner-clustering visually (iHeart/Cumulus/Hubbard cluster at the bottom).
des_05.rationale: A 29-row leaderboard gives readers a station they can find from their own city, which makes the data personal.

des_06.label: US map — 17 cities, 29 dots, sized by women's b2b %

content.initial_state: Dark grayscale tile layer (Carto Dark Matter via CDN). 29 city markers (multiple per city where >1 station) sized by b2b_women_pct (radius 4–18px) and colored on a red-white scale (red = lowest, white = highest). KKGO and WUBE labeled directly on the map.
content.transition: popup shows station name, owner, exact b2b_women %, and a one-line ranking
content.payoff: Reader sees the geographic spread is fairly even — bad rates are not regional, they are owner-driven

des_06.brief: Leaflet.js dark-themed interactive US map. Coordinates are hard-coded in JS for the 16 cities (Austin, Charlotte, Chicago, Cincinnati, Columbus, Dallas, Greensboro, Houston, Indianapolis, Kansas City, Los Angeles, Nashville, Philadelphia, San Antonio, Tampa, Washington DC). Each station is a dot. Where a city has multiple stations, jitter dots slightly. KKGO (LA) is the only big white dot on the West Coast; WUBE (Cincinnati) is the smallest, deepest red dot in the Midwest. Provide a fallback PNG (us_radio_map.png already generated) inside a <noscript> or as the loading state.
des_06.rationale: The data is geographic at the city level; flattening 17 cities into a bar chart wastes that dimension. A map lets readers find their own metro and feel the rule applied locally.

des_07.label: Owner cluster chart — small multiples or grouped bar

content.interaction: hover shows aggregate counts (b2b_women_count, total_plays, women_airplay_pct)

style.annotation: iHeart and Cumulus together = 13 of 29 stations

des_07.brief: Horizontal bars per owner, sorted ascending. Each bar shows the owner's portfolio b2b-women % and the number of stations they own (e.g., 'iHeartMedia (8 stations)'). Annotate 'iHeart + Cumulus = 13 of 29 stations' as a callout. Color the smallest owners (Mount Wilson, Cox) in tomato red to emphasize the inverted relationship.
des_07.rationale: Showing owner alongside station count reveals the consolidation story: bigger consolidator → stricter rule.

des_08.label: Daypart radial chart — when women come on, it's late

content.interaction: hover wedge to show count + hours + label; clock face has hour markings 12-3-6-9

des_08.brief: A 24-hour clock-face radial chart. Five wedges sized by share of women's b2b plays: OVN (12am-6am, big red), EVE (7pm-12am, medium red), AMD/MID/PMD (drive-time, small grey). The visual literally shows 'when women come on, it's the dark hours of the clock.' Annotate '63.4% of women's b2b plays land off-peak.'
des_08.rationale: A clock metaphor maps daypart→time-of-day directly, making the 'overnight exile' finding intuitive without reading axis labels.

des_09.label: Overnight studio image — atmospheric companion

content.prompt: Cinematic photo: empty late-night radio control room. Glowing VU meters and analog mixing board, single overhead lamp, digital clock reads 3:00 AM, blurred bokeh of city lights through a window. Mood: lonely, off-peak.

des_09.brief: Place this photo to the right of (or above) the radial daypart chart. The image shows an empty 3am studio — wordlessly answering 'who is listening when women are played together?' The answer: nobody.
des_09.rationale: Pairs an evocative still with the daypart chart so the off-peak finding feels like a place, not a category.

des_10.label: Women of color — 27 plays visualization

content.initial_state: A grid of 10,000 small dots representing every ~18 plays in the dataset (182,848 / 18 ≈ 10,158). Most dots are dim warm gray (men) or muted (mixed/white women).
content.transition: Animation: 1.5 dots fade to red — the 27 plays of women of color (each red dot = one play, scaled to fit the grid). After 2 seconds another animation highlights ZERO of those red dots are adjacent — there are no back-to-back pairs.
content.payoff: Reader sees the literal sparseness — 27 red specks across a near-uniform field, not a single one beside another.

des_10.brief: Procedurally drawn dot grid (Canvas or SVG). 27 red dots scattered randomly across a field of ~10,000 dim dots. After a beat, a subtle pulse animation fires to confirm 'no two red dots are touching' — that's the b2b=0 finding. Below the grid: stat-callout '27 plays · 0 back-to-back pairs.'
des_10.rationale: 27 plays out of 182,848 is hard to feel as a number. A visual where the eye must hunt for the red dots makes the sparseness viscerally felt.

des_11.label: Catalogue mix — Gold/Recurrent/Current 100% bar

content.interaction: hover segment shows label + count + pct

des_11.brief: A single horizontal stacked bar split 33% Gold, 45% Recurrent, 22% Current. Annotate 'Reba & Shania get to share air. The new women don't.'
des_11.rationale: A 100% stacked bar is the cleanest way to show share-of-mix when the question is 'when this happens, what kind is it?'

des_12.label: Per-station gap dot plot — men minus women

content.interaction: hover shows both b2b-men % and b2b-women %, the gap, and ratio

des_12.brief: 29 horizontal dumbbells, one per station. Left dot: b2b-women % (red, microscopic, often hugging the y-axis). Right dot: b2b-men % (tan, ~60-70). The connecting line shows the gap. Sort by gap descending so KFKF-FM is at top. The visual scrunch of all 29 red dots into a column on the left — vs the stretched-out men dots — IS the finding.
des_12.rationale: A dumbbell makes the within-station asymmetry visible at every row. You see, station by station, two values at honest scale.

des_13.label: Closing image — empty stage

content.prompt: Black and white documentary still: a single empty wooden chair on stage in front of a microphone, dim spotlight from above, deep shadow surrounding. No audience visible. Mood: absence, silence, exclusion.

des_13.brief: Full-bleed at the close. The empty chair on a country stage is the visual coda: who's not on the radio is who's not on the stage.
des_13.rationale: Closes the piece on an emotional, not numerical, beat — matching the editor's note 'leave them sitting with the imagery.'

des_14.label: Tomato salad metaphor image (mid-piece)

content.prompt: Editorial photo: a wooden salad bowl with mostly lettuce and a single small red tomato off-center. Overhead 45-degree shot, golden-hour kitchen lighting. References the 2015 Tomato-gate scandal.

des_14.brief: Place inline next to the Tomato-gate context paragraph. The salad-with-one-tomato is the literal image of the consultant's quote.
des_14.rationale: Anchors the abstract 'Tomato-gate' name in a concrete picture so the metaphor carries through the rest of the piece.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial / investigative — warm bone-white type on near-black, with two accent colors: tomato red (#C0392B) for women and warm tan (#C8A165) for men
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first hook → text/chart alternation in the body → image close. Charts never appear two in a row without a still image, callout, or interactive between them.
page_rhythm.centrepiece: des_05 (29-station leaderboard) and des_06 (interactive map) together form the audit table — they are the data centerpiece. des_teaser is the emotional centerpiece.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Display serif (e.g. 'Playfair Display' or 'Cormorant') for headline + stat callouts at 96px / 72px. Body in 'Inter' or system-ui at 17px / 1.65 line height. Section dividers as a thin tomato-red rule. Pull-quote treatment for Hill's 'lettuce in our salad' — italic serif, set into the page like a magazine.
